messages:
Alice Nguyen: Hey team, customer acme-inc reporting intermittent 429s from our API between 10:05-10:12 PST. They included one request id but we need a timeline + full headers to triage.
Ravi Patel: Can we ask them for the raw response headers, full request ids, and a curl that reproduces the failure? Also check if they have a client-side rate limiter.
Alice Nguyen: Yep. Can someone write a minimal repro checklist for the customer? :eyes:
Sarah (support-bot): Quick checklist for customer collection:
  1) failing curl (verbose) with the exact headers they send
  2) full response body + response headers for each 429
  3) HAR export or tcpdump of the session if possible
  4) exact timestamps (ISO) and timezone for each attempt
  5) app/client logs around the requests (include concurrency/backoff config)
  6) any rate-limit headers seen (`x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, `x-ratelimit-reset`, `x-request-id`)
  7) debug bundle (we'll provide upload link)
Ravi Patel: Also include which deployment they're hitting (hosted vs dedicated), the model name, and whether they're streaming responses. Add token counts if available.
Jake (sre): From our side include proxy/nginx request_ids and ingress latency metrics. We'll need to map their client ids to our internal ids for correlation.
Alice Nguyen: Pasting a curl template for them to run (ask them to increment X-Request-Id per attempt):
```bash
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -H 'X-Request-Id: TEST-REQ-1234' \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"hello world","max_tokens":10}'
```
Ravi Patel: Tell them to run the curl with `-v` and capture both stdout and stderr. If they get a 429, save the full response and headers. If they have retries, ask them to show retry timing.
Alice Nguyen: Customer replied with three request ids: TEST-REQ-1234, TEST-REQ-1256, TEST-REQ-1299. They attached a HAR and one raw response body.
Sarah (support-bot): Optional: run `curl --trace-ascii trace.txt ...` to capture TLS handshake and raw frames. If using Node/python, include snippet of code and concurrency level.
Jake (sre): I can pull our logs for those ids once we have the exact ISO timestamps. I'll query ingress -> router -> quota service logs (±2 minutes).
Ravi Patel: If this is a burst/retry pattern, we need the client's concurrency and backoff policy — that often causes quota window exhaustion quickly.
Alice Nguyen: I'll upload their HAR + curl outputs and send them a presigned link for debug bundle upload. Tagging @Jake (sre) to run log pulls when bundle is available. :+1:
Jake (sre): Roger. Once bundle + timestamps are in, I'll correlate: client X-Request-Id -> nginx id -> backend id -> quota decision entry. Will produce a short timeline and flag quota window hits or misattributed retries.
Alice Nguyen: Thanks all — I'll update thread after the upload.
